audit_findings.title: Expiring tax credit creates a recurring earnings headwind
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 jobs tax credits were $41.992 million, principally WOTC, equal to 3.1% of the $1,368.9 million OE anchor; the 1.1-point year-over-year increase in the H1 2026 effective tax rate equates to $14.5 million on $1,317.559 million of pretax income
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher post-expiration effective tax rate reduces after-tax OE and the earnings available to support modeled growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Absent reauthorization, the Company will experience a significant negative impact to the effective tax rate in future years.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax headwind is demonstrated, but a valuation error is not: H1 2026 results already reflect expired credits, so the latest OE includes at least part of the effect. Even the entire 2025 jobs-credit amount is only 3.1% of anchor OE and would lower values that are already below the $133.21 market price in every scenario. That scale is not sufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized OE using a post-expiration effective tax rate, identify how much of the H1 2026 effect is already included in the $1,516.5 million latest OE, and rerun all scenarios without double-counting it.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include operating rather than distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,589.59 million July 2026 cash add-back, equal to $7.06 per diluted share and 7.6% of base equity value; January 2026 processor receivables were $107.5 million, while captive and minimum operating cash are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-distributable cash included in the equity bridge directly overstates equity value and value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Payments due from processors for electronic tender transactions classified as cash and cash equivalents totaled approximately $ 107.5 million and $ 94.4 million at January 30, 2026 and January 31, 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that consolidated cash contains at least operating settlement receivables and that the captive insurer must maintain regulatory liquidity. The known $107.5 million item alone is only about $0.48 per share, but the valuation has not established that any of the full $1,589.59 million balance is excess. Because the amount at risk is 7.6% of base equity value, the unresolved classification is material even though removing cash would reinforce, rather than reverse, the current below-market conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 31, 2026 cash composition, captive statutory-capital requirement, restrictions, processor receivables and minimum operating-liquidity analysis; rerun the bridge using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Supplier finance may be an omitted debt-like claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $406.3 million outstanding at July 31, 2026, equal to $1.80 per diluted share and 2.0% of the $20,823 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If normalized working-capital requirements are absent from OE, the financing-supported amount could require a bridge deduction or reduction of excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 30, 2026 and January 31, 2025, the amount of obligations outstanding that the Company has confirmed with the financial institutions under the supply chain finance program were $ 385.2 million and $ 399.7 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The program and balance are demonstrated, but an omission is not: the obligations remain recorded in accounts payable or accrued expenses, and supplier participation does not alter Dollar General's payment obligation. Even deducting the full July balance as an additional claim would reduce base value from $92.43 to approximately $90.63 per share, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. A working-capital normalization issue remains possible but is not large enough on the filed balance to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $406.3 million to accounts payable and accrued expenses, confirm how working-capital changes enter each historical OE observation, and run a full-balance deduction sensitivity to verify the approximately $1.80-per-share bound.

audit_findings.title: Projected reinvestment may exceed the burden embedded in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 projected capex of $1.4-$1.5 billion exceeds 2025 actual capex of $1,241.2 million by $158.8-$258.8 million, or 11.6%-18.9% of the $1,368.9 million OE anchor; H1 2026 capex was $758.45 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance, remodel or replacement spending omitted from the OE charge reduces OE directly and may also make the modeled growth rates unattainable without additional reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures during 2026 are projected to be in the range of $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending level is demonstrated, but the filing does not classify the projected amount between recurring maintenance and discretionary expansion, so an OE error is not yet demonstrated. The incremental spending is nevertheless large relative to anchor OE: if recurring, it would absorb 11.6%-18.9% of the anchor before capitalization and could materially alter scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1.4-$1.5 billion forecast into maintenance, replacement, Project Elevate, Project Renovate, relocation, expansion, supply-chain and technology uses; compare the recurring portion with the charge embedded in each OE year and rerun all scenarios net of any shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued litigation could create a claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured settlement or remediation payment would reduce OE when incurred or require a probability-weighted claim deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For some matters, a liability is not probable or the amount cannot be reasonably estimated and therefore an accrual has not been made.
audit_findings.explanation: No present valuation error is demonstrated merely because accounting recognition was not warranted. The July 2026 filing still states that the securities-litigation loss or range cannot be estimated, while also acknowledging that an adverse outcome could be material. With no claimed-loss estimate, probability or insurance recovery in the record, the potential value effect cannot be quantified or classified as presently material.
audit_findings.action: Review case developments through September 5, 2026, claimed damages, dismissal-stage outcomes, insurance limits, exclusions and indemnification; if a defensible probability and loss range emerge, calculate a probability-weighted after-tax claim and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Self-insurance reserves could understate recurring claim costs
audit_findings.magnitude: potential shortfall unquantified; filed reserve was $377.601 million at January 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse claim development would increase recurring SG&A and reduce OE; captive cash required to support the exposure must also be excluded from excess cash in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If future claim trends deviate from recent historical patterns, or other unanticipated events affect the number and significance of future claims, we may be required to record additional expenses or expense reductions, which could be material to our future financial results.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing describes forward-looking estimation risk, not a demonstrated reserve deficiency. The $377.601 million reserve was audited as a critical audit matter using actuarial specialists and an independently developed range, and management states that its actuarial estimates have been materially accurate. The record supplies no July reserve balance, adverse development or amount outside the actuarial range, so this is a monitoring item rather than a current valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 2026 reserve balance, actuarial range, paid-loss and incurred-loss development by coverage year, and captive regulatory-cash requirement; reopen and rerun OE or the cash bridge if subsequent development shows a systematic deficiency.
